script: Spread and total were not saved for HOU at IND, so the script is form-only: the Houston Texans have lived through Dalton Schultz (22 targets, 175 yards, 130 air yards) with C.J. Stroud at +0.39 EPA vs blitz and -0.13 without it, while the Indianapolis Colts have lived on Jonathan Taylor (43 carries, 190 yards) and Josh Downs (13 targets, 109 yards) with Daniel Jones at -0.22 EPA when the Houston Texans do not blitz.
who_goes_off: Houston Texans TE Dalton Schultz should go off against the Indianapolis Colts: 175 yards on 22 targets already, and the IND defense allows 11.88 YPA on 17 middle attempts, the zone Schultz works, into a 25% IND blitz where Stroud is +0.39 EPA (n=20). Indianapolis Colts RB Jonathan Taylor should go off on volume, 43 carries for 190 yards, even into a Houston Texans run defense that allows 4.12 YPC.
weak_spot: The Indianapolis Colts' real weak spot is the middle (11.88 YPA, 17 att) and left (11.0 YPA, 22 att), plus a run front at 5.67 YPC with 10 runs of 10-plus; IND's right side is the only pass area at 8.19 YPA (32 att). The Houston Texans leak the middle (10.47 YPA, 17 att) and right (10.82 YPA, 28 att), while HOU's left is 4.0 YPA on 15 attempts and HOU has allowed only 5 runs of 10-plus.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for HOU at IND, so neither the Houston Texans nor the Indianapolis Colts have an injury fallout to price; Nico Collins's 10 targets and 75 yards for Houston stay in the form sample only.
qb_vs_blitz: Houston Texans QB C.J. Stroud is +0.39 EPA vs blitz (n=20) and -0.13 unblitzed, and the Indianapolis Colts blitz 25%, so about a quarter of HOU dropbacks hit Stroud's good split and feed Dalton Schultz. Indianapolis Colts QB Daniel Jones is -0.02 vs blitz (n=19) and -0.22 with no blitz, and the Houston Texans blitz only 17%, so Jones spends most of HOU@IND in the worse split and Tyler Warren's 10 air yards get no blitz boost.

picks.why: Houston Texans TE Dalton Schultz has 175 receiving yards on 22 targets and 130 air yards through two games, about 87.5 a game, against a 49.5 line, and the Indianapolis Colts allow 11.88 YPA on 17 middle throws while IND blitzes 25% into Stroud's +0.39 EPA blitz split.

Indianapolis Colts TE Tyler Warren has 12 targets for 34 yards and 10 air yards, about 17 a game, against a 46.5 line, and the Houston Texans' 17% blitz rate leaves Daniel Jones in his -0.22 EPA unblitzed split while Colts WR Josh Downs (109 yards on 13 targets) is the IND receiver actually separating.
